lesson.title: A method for reading prohibitions
lesson.summary: Read the regulated action and every prohibition element before comparing high-risk duties.

prerequisites.reason: Market and service triggers depend on the supply actions and actors defined earlier.
The detailed distinction develops the initial separation between classification and permission.
The distinction needs a prior definition of high-risk classification.

blocks: A **regulated action** is what a prohibition restricts: placing on the market, putting into service, use, or a specifically qualified combination. Read the action in the relevant point.

Some Article 5 points qualify supply by a specific purpose; the real-time remote-identification point restricts use in a particular setting. Do not replace these distinctions with 'all development is banned'. Scope exclusions still need their own test.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1), 5(8); Article 6; Article 113

blocks: **Prohibition elements** are the conditions that must be examined together. A point may specify a technique, people affected, context, effect or harm, plus an exception or qualification.
Northbridge's practical table gives each element its own evidence and records unknowns. A troubling product label may justify investigation, but does not substitute for showing the legal elements.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1), 5(8); Article 6; Article 113

blocks: **Prohibited versus high-risk** separates two legal questions. A permitted practice can be high-risk and have requirements. A prohibited practice does not become permitted by meeting a high-risk checklist.
A human reviewer, consent assertion, warning label or certificate is not a universal exception. Read the exact point to see whether and how it matters.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1), 5(8); Article 6; Article 113

blocks: Also record the application date and other-law limits. Most original Chapter II rules apply from 2 February 2025; specified new provisions apply from 2 December 2026. Article 5(8) preserves prohibitions arising under other Union law.
Our fictional cases test specified elements. Their conclusions are tied to those facts and dates; they do not authorise an actual deployment or settle every related legal issue.

questions.prompt: A reviewer says Article 5 bans every form of research and development. What should be checked?

options.blocks: The exact regulated action and relevant scope provisions

options.reason: That does not establish the statutory action.

options.blocks: Only the phrase 'AI ban' in a headline
options.reason: A headline collapses the legal distinctions.
